orders.thesis: Post-earnings capitulation (-27% on 10/29 on cRPO guide 18.5% vs ~19.5% Street, first EPS miss) has based for 4 sessions at 106-112, up 3% Tuesday, with software swept by AI-disruption fear that looks overdone given AI ACV +65% and a raised $1.7B target. Broad tech stabilising (XLK +1.3%, futures up after midterms removed political risk). Small size because the sector trend is still unproven and negative post-earnings drift is a real risk.

summary: Session 2026-11-04 (pre-open). Tuesday close: SPY +0.30%, QQQ +0.62%, XLK +1.31% (first up day after a -6.9% 5-day drop). Democrats swept both chambers in the midterms; futures rose after early losses. After-hours/premarket gaps: AMD +6-7% (Q4 guide ~$17B beat), ANET +12% (guide beat), SMCI +9%, AMGN -2 to -3% (biosimilar worries), BKNG down (revenue miss), SHOP -8.7% Tuesday, UBER -2% premarket (Q4 EPS guide 0.95-0.99 vs 1.06 Street; driver shortages, Middle East, AV spend; Q3 EPS slight miss). CVS announced a split into two companies by 2028; KHC to divest its NA coffee business. I did not chase the earnings gaps because they are priced in at the open. Opened a small 5% NOW long at about 112 as a stabilisation rebound: stop -9%, target +16%, horizon 12 days, p=0.52. The idea is a base at 106-112 after the -27% drop, and the AI-disruption fear in software looks overdone. Next session: check NOW's open and whether tech (FTNT 128, INTC 60.5, GOOGL 280, RDDT 96) keeps rebounding. If the market makes a second up close, consider adding to the rebound longs, but only with a catalyst. Also check whether Uber's weakness continues (drift short candidate) and CVS split reaction. Lesson so far: 4 cash sessions avoided losses in the knife-catching phase, but cash earns nothing, so small positions are fine once the tape stabilises.
